[indications_and_usage]
Use • treats frequent heartburn (occurs 2 or more days a week) • not intended for immediate relief of heartburn; this drug may take 1 to 4 days for full effect

[dosage_and_administration]
Directions • for adults 18 years of age and older • this product is to be used once a day (every 24 hours), every day for 14 days • it may take 1 to 4 days for full effect; some people get complete relief of symptoms within 24 hours 14-Day Course of Treatment • swallow 1 tablet with a glass of water before eating in the morning • take every day for 14 days • do not take more than 1 tablet a day • do not use for more than 14 days unless directed by your doctor • swallow whole. Do not chew or crush tablets Repeated 14-Day Courses (if needed) • you may repeat a 14-day course every 4 months • do not take for more than 14 days or more often than every 4 months unless directed by a doctor • children under 18 years of age: ask a doctor. Heartburn in children may sometimes be caused by a serious condition.

user: What are the most common adverse reactions to Omeprazole?
response:
{"answer": "The label excerpt provided does not include information about adverse reactions to this omeprazole product. However, based on standard pharmacology knowledge of omeprazole, the most common adverse reactions typically include:

• Headache (most frequent, occurring in 5-7% of patients)
• Diarrhea
• Nausea
• Abdominal pain
• Constipation
• Vomiting
• Flatulence

Less common but notable adverse reactions include:
• Dizziness
• Rash
• Elevated liver enzymes
• Hypomagnesemia (with chronic use)

Chronic use considerations:
• Long-term omeprazole use may reduce absorption of vitamin B12, calcium, and magnesium
• Risk of Clostridioides difficile infection with prolonged use
• Potential increased fracture risk with long-term therapy

For complete and accurate adverse reaction information specific to this product, you should consult the full prescribing information label or package insert. This over-the-counter product is indicated for short-term use (14-day courses), so serious adverse events would be rare at this dosing regimen. If patients experience unusual symptoms or need extended therapy beyond the labeled 14-day course, they should contact their healthcare provider."}
